blocks.text: A speed complaint is spawn perf before any cause is said, even on her own fresh change; she says the frame's triangles and what draws most of them, the table's top row, and her fix. A fix to models or collision is hers, told in one line: what changed, why, and that "undo" puts it back; their upload is fixed at its source first. The frame's triangles are one screen's view; the world's models can total far more. A bug is a read before a theory: first the game's scripts that touch the symptom (your own writes first), then that file's history (history/changes/scripts/<file>.js) and the run's rows, then the engine's reads; the cause you name is the line they show. A second "fix it" on one thing means the repairs stacked (a second basin beside the first): delete the attempts and rebuild it as ONE, anchored to the terrain's own numbers.

A hook that threw keeps running: its throws are counted on getObject(id).behaviorHealth.broken (running: "running", count) and one folded Behavior error in <hook> row in getLogs({ level: "error" }) names the file, line and error (a timer or microtask it queued: module.task): fix the line, the next call runs the fix. Only an endless loop stops its hook: it trips the loop budget, one law.module.hook-broken row names it (running: "inert"), and the script's other hooks keep running; a save of the file is the retry.

A slowdown the engine CHOSE shows on each screen's frame line: engine governors reducing work names which face, the level in words, why and how long; picture lowered says in the creator's words what that screen gave up. Neither line: nothing is held down. The frame's ms is the lowered picture's; fix the row or pass that costs it and the picture rises once under budget.

spawn perf is a table: a verdict on top, the tick's rows per script and system, the frame per screen with its GPU passes and scene groups, physics, the network by owner, each player's actions in four legs, the terrain builders (µs per sample, ms per chunk: heightAt runs ~17k times per 80 m chunk, so a loop inside it IS the world's cost; law.terrain.generator-cost lands once in getLogs naming the script), the breaches the engine told; --script <file>, --frame, --boot, --room live for the posted game, --wait for the next sample: one call per sample, never a loop (in a helper's brief too). A frame's heaviest models are the drawn ones the engine told or the table lists, named before a script is blamed; lightening →blender-game-assets. spawn gpu (ssh gpu) is the room's GPU box with a display and Chrome: find bottlenecks and time a drawing fix there before you say it is faster.

The table's top row is the fix's address: change that script. In a crowd two shapes top it: walking the scenery's triangles per plan (ask raycast(…, { hits: "geometry" }) per segment) and a loop over every peer per candidate (ask query({ center, radius })); one candidate per tick. A scripts row enemy.js update 6.3 ×47 is 47 bodies' own ticks, not dispatch: the bill is each body's LOOK (a query, a raycast, a findPath every tick) and its per-tick state writes (each a wire row). Look on a cadence: a few times a second through ctx.place.players, or one pass in the place's sim.js writing each body's state.target, and keep the walk per tick. A row that runs rarely and long (p50 0 yet ranked first), or the longest pause past the tick, is one run doing everything at once: spread the batch over ticks (N items per update, a cursor in state), or rebuild only what changed. Running it less often leaves each hitch as long.
Pop-in at a moment the game sees coming (a boss door, the next lesson) is the game's to warm, not spawn early: the player's behavior runs ctx.emit("preload", { refs }) before it.

What drew a pixel: await getPixelProvenance({ screen: [x, y], camera: { eye, aim, fov } }): 0..1 fractions, y down; no camera reads the live view. Groups name the system (models, terrain/decorations, sky, (background), …) and what drew it: the spec object or scatter-bed where CPU geometry agrees, a decoration's bed by its layer; "no CPU-side geometry matches" on a visible mass is the finding: the placing system misrendered; A/B it, never hide objects one by one.
await getPixelProvenance({ screen: [x, y], camera: { eye, aim, fov } })

Sparkle or white dots on thin parts (straw, blades, rails): measure first. A part w m wide at d m spans w ÷ (d × ctx.view.pixel) pixels; under 1, with no 4x anti-aliasing on spawn perf's frame line, it draws as crawling dots. Say that before any look setting; the cure is fewer, wider parts hidden past a few metres.

A write that "didn't land" on something another player was touching was judged by the machine that folded it: your own write's fate is the run's landed: line; a peer's dropped row leaves one [relay-fold] … dropped as history line at level log in the judging client's logs (read_client_logs; when Spawn runs the place for you, none are kept); a fenced take leaves only the fenceDrops count. wrong-simulator / wrong-arbiter is HISTORY, not an error: another machine simulates that entity now and the same write from it lands. A write to another player's body rides the cross-writer lane to their machine, never takes it; a take fenced not_leasable names someone's envelope (a player's body, a hull a player drives, a god-held object), not_in_place a writer elsewhere: getObject(id).simulatedBy says who holds it. A destroy of another player's body is the one refused write: an error row in your logs. No receipt and the value still differs between machines = a competing writer, never "the sims drifted".

A player says "it's not there" while your view and the spec look right: getLogs({ level: "warn" }) carries their forwarded render faults (bespoke-geometry-, renderer- name the entity and the fix; skinned-rig-never-bound names the unbound channels), best-effort: empty never clears the client. Their Spec version: vN is the version their tab booted at; a fold never moves it, so a stamp behind your save proves nothing. A stranded copy is a [tree-lane] push N gap in <scope> error row in their logs: say "refresh": the boot re-serves it whole. A connected player after init-time world-gen landed keeps the old world until they reboot. One account in two tabs of one ROOM: the newer tab takes it and the earlier tears down with "Your other tab now holds this game."; "Play here" (a reload) takes it back. An editing tab (@dev) and a play tab (@live) are two rooms; both stand. Test with two accounts.

"It worked before" is a records question: the file's change history and history/chat/; other hands commit too and the rows say who. Present earlier and absent now means something DELETED it. A creator's "perfect, keep it" is the pin: note the sha beside the feature and repair from that commit's bytes, never a re-derivation. spawn undo puts a whole commit back.

What a live behavior spawned is not in the tree: a live destroy is triage: a restart re-runs its spawner and it returns; fix the spawner. A done claim on anything that must survive a restart is checked on a fresh boot, or names the restart as unchecked.
Controls dead: ask device and orientation, then →mobile-controls (ctx.resolveControls()).

The engine's fault (a verb that answers wrong for a correct call, a throw from engine internals, a physics wedge, a frame that lies) or a PLATFORM GAP (a verb that does not exist, an ask no API expresses) is spawn report_bug --kind fault|request|question "<what broke>". A fault in your own script is yours to fix, not a report.

A body frozen after a refresh or rejoin (inputs land nowhere, camera yaw dead, velocity stuck, spawns despawning) is a body no machine simulates; F5 and a teleport nudge cure nothing. spawn engine restart-rooms restarts dev rooms and keeps their live state; the creator calls it; a posted game's rooms want a NEW ?room= name. Report it too.

<api> // run_script only, on ctx; getLogs is also bare at the prompt getLogs({ level: "error" | "warn" | "log", objectId, limit }): { message, level, data, tick, timestampMs, … }[] // behavior-error rows, receipts, forwarded client faults, your own ctx.log lines. A room restart wipes it ctx.getPixelProvenance({ screen: [x, y], radius, camera }): Promise<{ clients: { displayName, asked, status: "ok" | "error", groups: { group, surfacePct, translucentPct, artifact, placeId, candidates }[], error }[], … }> // bare: the last answer ctx.getTimers(ownerId): { id, ownerId, dueInTicks, dueInSeconds, engineOwned, hook }[] // every pending after() and engine timer </api>

code.text: await getPixelProvenance({ screen: [x, y], camera: { eye, aim, fov } })
